metadata.description: Accepted, independently verified entries — the production lexicon. Includes contested entries (gloss null) that present scholarly uncertainty to the reader.
metadata.score_range: 1-5, all axes now scored (surprise null for contested entries, which carry no gloss)
metadata.forms: Optional per-entry list of derived words sharing the entry's etymon (governor -> govern, government). Each form has word, gloss, part_of_speech, verification_source, and optional plural / surprise_score overrides; everything else is inherited from the parent entry.

entries.note: apo 'away' + kalyptein 'to cover'; a revealing, not a catastrophe.
ad + rīpa 'riverbank, shore'.
diminutive of astēr 'star'.
avis 'bird' + specere 'to watch'; omens were read from the flight of birds.

entries.editorial_notes: Traceable to Proto-Germanic *bruthiz, but the pre-Germanic origin remains uncertain/disputed.

entries.note: Modern -groom is folk-etymological.
diminutive of bouge, from Latin bulga 'leather bag'.
Using calculi on counting boards.
entries.editorial_notes: Recovers the abacus/counting-board practice.

entries.note: Pebble used for reckoning.
Later developed 'frank'.
entries.editorial_notes: candidus core sense is 'white / bright / dazzling'.

entries.note: White toga of office-seekers.
entries.editorial_notes: Recovers the Roman electoral practice of the whitened toga.

entries.note: caput 'head'; wealth once reckoned by head of cattle.
cancellī 'lattice, grating'; an official stationed at the screened barrier of a court.
kharassein 'to engrave'; originally a stamping tool.
klinē 'bed'.
Latin cuneus 'wedge'; the wedge-shaped die that stamped metal.
komē 'hair'; named for its trailing tail.
com + panis 'bread'.
com + grex 'flock'; a gathering into one flock.
com + sidus 'star'; an astrological/augural metaphor.
currere 'to run'; money kept in circulation.
kyōn 'dog'; the Cynics' shameless, dog-like way of life.
Flower opens by day.
de + caedere 'to cut'.
decimus 'tenth'; the Roman punishment of executing every tenth soldier.
de + līra 'furrow'; a plowman straying from the furrow.
de + sidus 'star'; to await what the stars bring.
diploun 'to fold'; official documents were folded in two.
Attributed to an unfavorable star.

ex + līmen 'threshold'.
enkyklios 'circular' + paideia 'education'; the full circle of liberal arts.
en 'in' + theos 'god'; the state of being possessed by a god.
exāmen 'the tongue of a balance'.
ex + onus 'burden, load'.
Proto-Germanic *fehu 'livestock, wealth'.

entries.note: Translation of evangelium.
god + sibb 'kin'.
entries.editorial_notes: OE sibb = kin generally; godsibb historically meant godparent/baptismal sponsor. 'God sibling' is the literal root recovery.

entries.note: kybernan 'to steer a ship', via Latin gubernator.
parallels 'pagan': open, uncultivated land set against the (Christian) town.
entries.editorial_notes: The heath-dweller theory is widely cited but the ultimate origin is not fully certain.

entries.note: hieros 'sacred' + arkhein 'to rule'; originally the ranked orders of angels.
Religious feast day.
entries.editorial_notes: Borderline transparent compound; confirm it still surprises.

entries.note: hospes 'host, guest, stranger'.
variant of ūmor 'liquid, moisture'.
hús 'house' + bóndi 'dweller/farmer'.
entries.editorial_notes: Inherited via OE hūsbonda, a calque of Old Norse húsbóndi (hús 'house' + bóndi 'dweller/freeholder').

entries.note: idios 'one's own, private'; a layman outside public office.
in + augurāre 'to act as augur'.
in + fluere 'to flow'; an astral fluid once thought to affect human affairs.
in + salīre 'to leap'.
hlaf 'loaf' + a second element traditionally linked to 'kneader/maker'.
entries.editorial_notes: Traditional analysis; verify second element before publication.

entries.note: hlaf 'loaf' + weard 'keeper'.
luna 'moon'; intermittent madness blamed on lunar phases.
manu 'by hand' + factura 'making'; originally literal.
entries.editorial_notes: Productive irony: now denotes machine/industrial production.

entries.note: manu 'by hand' + scriptus 'written'.
entries.editorial_notes: Attested in Medieval Latin, not Classical; manu 'by hand' + scriptus 'written'.

entries.note: From a Germanic compound (marah 'horse' + skalk 'servant').
entries.editorial_notes: Ultimately from Frankish/Germanic *marhskalk (marh 'horse' + skalk 'servant'); Old French mareschal is the proximate source.

entries.note: melas 'black' + kholē 'bile'.
medius + diēs 'mid-day'.
minus 'less'; a subordinate or servant.
mort 'dead' + gage 'pledge'.
Diminutive of mus 'mouse'.
named for Mosul, the Iraqi city that produced the cloth.
mare is a supernatural being that sits on the sleeper's chest.
Greek nostos 'homecoming' + algos 'pain'.
entries.editorial_notes: Coined 1688 as a medical term.

entries.note: nose + hole.
Enclosed place of plants.
entries.editorial_notes: First element ('ort-') is disputed; verify before promotion.

entries.note: ostrakon 'potsherd, tile'; Athenians voted exile by scratching a name onto broken pottery.
pāgus 'rural district'; Christian townsfolk's term for rustic non-believers.
entries.editorial_notes: A rival theory reads pāgānus as 'civilian' (one not enlisted as God's soldier); both trace to pagus.

entries.note: Pan, the god whose sudden cry was said to stampede herds.
present participle of patī 'to suffer, endure'.
From pecus 'cattle'; wealth measured in livestock.
entries.editorial_notes: Recovers wealth-as-livestock economy.

entries.note: quills were cut from feathers.
diminutive of pēniculus, itself of pēnis 'tail'; the earliest pencils were brushes.
originally an actor's mask, possibly via Etruscan phersu.
prex 'prayer'; held only at another's pleasure.
prae 'before' + sedēre 'to sit'.
prae + vāricāre 'to straddle'.
pyr 'fire' + mania 'madness'; an irresistible compulsion to burn.
quaranta 'forty'; the Venetian plague-isolation period.
rīvus 'brook, stream'; those sharing a watercourse became competitors.
from sal 'salt'; Roman greens were dressed in brine.
Avoid the 'paid in salt' myth; connected to salt provision/allowance.

entries.note: sancīre 'to make sacred, ratify'.
sanguis 'blood'; the cheerful humor.
sarx 'flesh'; a biting remark that strips flesh like a dog.
sarx 'flesh' + phagein 'to eat'; a limestone believed to consume corpses.
feminine of salsus 'salted', from sal 'salt'.
idle time devoted to learning and discussion.
Shire officer.
spin + -ster; the traditional occupation of unmarried women.
stige 'climbing' + rap 'rope'; original mounting strap.

entries.note: super + cilium 'eyelid'.
kheir 'hand' + ergon 'work'.
sykon 'fig' + phainein 'to show'.
entries.editorial_notes: No scholarly consensus on origin. Leading theories include an obscene fig-gesture, fig-thieving informers, and other unproven accounts.

entries.note: syn + ballein 'to throw'; a token split in two and compared to verify identity.
named for al-ʿAttābiya, the Baghdad district that wove striped silk.
from Latin tālea 'rod, stick'; debts were recorded by notches.
texere 'to weave'; a woven fabric of words.
diminutive of toile 'cloth'; originally a dressing-cloth.
tragos 'goat' + ōidē 'song'; likely tied to goat-costumed satyr performers or a goat prize.
tribulum 'threshing sledge'; affliction as a grinding-down.
tribūnus 'tribal officer'; the raised seat of judgment.
tri + via 'road'; a trivium was a common meeting-place, hence commonplace.
vērus 'true' + dictum 'saying'.
vindr 'wind' + auga 'eye'.
